subject: Archaeology
title: Portable XRF: Chemistry in the Field
description: A 60-second lesson on Portable XRF: Chemistry in the Field.

hook.text: A handheld device reads the chemistry of any artifact in 30 seconds, right on site.

buildup.text: Portable XRF guns fire X-rays at an object. The returning signal reveals its elements.

discovery.text: Archaeologists identify obsidian sources and pigment origins without sending samples to a lab.

twist.text: pXRF is non-destructive. Nothing is scraped or chipped. The artifact stays intact.

climax.text: At Pompeii, pXRF found invisible paint on statues. Roman sculptures were brightly colored.

punchline.text: Roman statues were never white. A handheld scanner proved it.

quiz.question: What did pXRF reveal about Roman marble statues?
options: They were made of a different stone than believed
Invisible paint traces showed they were originally brightly colored
The marble was imported from Egypt rather than quarried locally

details.summary: Portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) analyzers let archaeologists determine the chemical composition of artifacts in the field without laboratory analysis. By pointing the device at pottery, obsidian, or metal, researchers instantly identify source materials and trade connections.
details.whyItMatters: Before pXRF, chemical analysis required sending samples to distant labs and waiting weeks. Handheld analyzers provide instant results on-site, allowing real-time decisions about what to excavate further and revealing trade networks on the spot.
takeaways: Portable XRF identifies artifact chemical composition instantly
It traces raw materials to their geological source regions
Real-time analysis speeds fieldwork decision-making dramatically

faq.question: How does portable XRF work?
faq.answer: The device fires X-rays at an object, which cause atoms to emit characteristic fluorescent X-rays. Each element produces a unique energy signature. The analyzer measures these energies to determine the elemental composition of the surface — all within seconds and without damaging the artifact.

faq.question: What archaeological questions can pXRF answer?
faq.answer: It identifies where obsidian tools came from by matching chemical fingerprints to volcanic sources. It determines ore sources for bronze and iron artifacts. It reveals whether pottery was made locally or imported. These answers map ancient trade routes and exchange networks.
